title: Tacoma Smelter Soil Area (Lead & Arsenic)
summary: Decades ago, smoke from the historic Tacoma smelter carried trace lead and arsenic particles north across South King County and West Seattle. While safe for everyday living, simple soil testing is recommended if you plan to garden or dig.

official_sources.name: WA Dept of Ecology DirtAlert Interactive Map
King County Public Health Lead & Toxics Program

title: Everett Smelter Soil Area
summary: Historic smelting in North Everett left trace lead and arsenic in local topsoil. Free state soil sampling programs are available for impacted residential properties.

official_sources.name: WA Dept of Ecology Everett Smelter Cleanup

title: Lower Duwamish Waterway Cleanup Zone
summary: A designated federal cleanup zone along the industrial Duwamish River focused on riverbed restoration and sediment safety.

official_sources.name: EPA Lower Duwamish Waterway Superfund Portal

title: Paine Field Flight Corridor (Noise & Air Quality)
summary: Neighborhoods surrounding Snohomish County Airport (Paine Field) experience commercial and aerospace jet activity. Flight paths and air quality monitoring are publicly tracked.

official_sources.name: Paine Field Airport Noise Program & Contour Maps
Puget Sound Clean Air Agency Monitoring

title: Sea-Tac Airport Flight Path Corridor
summary: Active arrival and departure flight paths for Seattle-Tacoma International Airport. Features sound insulation programs and continuous regional air quality monitoring.

official_sources.name: Port of Seattle Sea-Tac Noise Programs Portal
Puget Sound Clean Air Agency Flight Corridor Air Study

title: Boeing Field / KBFI Flight Path Corridor
summary: King County International Airport (Boeing Field) serves heavy cargo, corporate jets, and test flights over South Seattle (Georgetown, Beacon Hill, South Park) and Tukwila.

official_sources.name: King County International Airport (Boeing Field) Portal

title: Local Municipal Airfields & General Aviation
summary: Proximity to regional airfields (Harvey Field, Renton Municipal, Arlington, Auburn) with private plane traffic and light aircraft flight patterns.

official_sources.name: FAA Airport Data & Flight Noise Guidelines

title: Puget Sound Bluff & Slope Management Zone
summary: Coastal bluffs and steep hillsides along Puget Sound require proper rainwater drainage and vegetation care to prevent soil erosion during winter rainstorms.

official_sources.name: WA Dept of Ecology Coastal Landslides & Bluffs Guide
WA DNR Landslide Hazards Portal

title: River Valley Floodplain & Channel Zone
summary: Low-lying properties near major river basins (Snoqualmie, Snohomish, Skykomish, Cedar) where winter heavy rain or snowmelt can cause high water events.

official_sources.name: King County Flood Warning System
Snohomish County Flood Services Portal

title: Puget Sound Marine Beach & Water Quality
summary: Seasonal advisories or swimming closures along public saltwater beaches due to rainfall runoff or marine red tide biotoxins.

official_sources.name: WA Dept of Health Shellfish & Beach Safety Map
SoundToxins Puget Sound Monitoring Network

title: Freshwater Lake Algae Bloom Watch
summary: Warm late-summer weather can cause temporary toxic blue-green algae blooms in popular lakes (Lake Washington, Green Lake, Lake Stevens).

official_sources.name: King County Lake Algae Watch Portal
WA Freshwater Algae Control Program

title: Foothill Glacial Soil (Radon Gas Risk)
summary: Odorless natural radon gas rising from deep glacial till, most common in valley and foothill towns. Easily tested with a $20 home kit and fixed with a basic fan system.

official_sources.name: WA Dept of Health Radon Testing & Mitigation Portal

title: Puget Sound Convergence Zone Weather Pattern
summary: A unique local atmospheric collision zone that brings localized heavy downpours, hail, or sudden winter snow bursts to parts of King and Snohomish counties.

official_sources.name: National Weather Service Seattle Forecast Office

title: Historic Underground Coal Mine Area
summary: Historic 19th and early 20th century coal mining tunnels in foothill communities (Newcastle, Renton, Issaquah, Black Diamond) that warrant a quick soil check.

official_sources.name: WA DNR Abandoned Mine Lands Portal

title: Lead-Based Paint Safety (Pre-1978 Homes)
summary: Homes built before 1978 require federal lead disclosures and lead-safe practices during remodels to prevent toxic dust.

official_sources.name: EPA Lead-Safe Certified Contractor Program
WA Dept of Health Lead Safety Portal

title: Asbestos Building Materials (Pre-1980 Homes)
summary: Homes constructed prior to 1980 often contain asbestos in popcorn ceilings, vinyl floor tiles, duct insulation, or transite piping.

official_sources.name: Puget Sound Clean Air Agency Asbestos Regulations

title: Moisture, Mold & PNW 'Attic Rain'
summary: High PNW winter humidity can cause warm indoor moisture to condense on cold roof sheathing (attic rain) or accumulate in unsealed crawl spaces.

official_sources.name: WA Dept of Health Mold & Moisture Control Guide

title: Underground Heating Oil Tank & PLIA Cleanup Grant
summary: Older oil heating systems may have buried fuel tanks. Washington's Pollution Liability Insurance Agency (PLIA) offers grants up to $75,000 for tank removal and soil cleanup.

official_sources.name: WA PLIA Heating Oil Loan & Grant Program (HOLG)

title: Private Well Water & Septic RSS Inspection Rules
summary: King and Snohomish counties require a formal Septic Report of System Status (RSS) prior to home sales, along with routine well water safety testing.

official_sources.name: King County Public Health ONSITE Septic Portal
Snohomish County On-Site Sewage RSS Program

title: WA Mandatory Resale Safety Compliance
summary: Washington law requires working smoke and carbon monoxide detectors inside/outside every bedroom and floor level, plus double-strapped water heaters anchored to studs.

official_sources.name: WA State Building Code Council Safety Guidelines
RCW 43.44.110 - Smoke Detection Devices Requirement
